subject: Surge safety lane and early payment incentive

Subject: Surge safety lane and early payment incentive

Hi Sanjay / Launchly procurement team,

Thanks again for the call yesterday — appreciate the transparency on traffic patterns for the May launch. To avoid capacity pain during the first 30 days we can offer a short-term "surge safety lane" that combines: a temporary quota buffer, a soft overrun rate tier, and an early-payment rebate to reduce net cost for ramp weeks. High level: 

- Duration: 30 days from go-live (one-time).
- Buffer: +30% of committed QPS / monthly quota provisioned as a warm pool (reserved for Launchly).
- Overrun pricing: blended overrun at 1.6x list rate for the first 50% of overrun, 2.4x beyond that (applies only to delta above committed quota + buffer).
- Early-payment incentive: 2% rebate on the overrun portion if invoice is paid within 10 days; or 3% if pre-paid at start of window (we can bake into a PO).
- Caps & guardrails: credits capped at 25% of the committed monthly invoice; autoscaling will prefer the warm pool first, then payg model variants as fallback.

I've attached a proposed pricing spreadsheet and a short provisioning plan that shows how the warm pool is carved and billed. If this looks viable we can issue a short addendum to your contract and route to procurement for PO/signature.

A couple of asks: could procurement confirm whether a 30-day prepay would be acceptable under your PO terms, and if so whether they prefer the 3% prepay rebate or the 2% quick-pay rebate? Also confirm billing contact and any required PO language.

Happy to jump on a short call to walk through the spreadsheet.

Thanks,

Hi Sanjay — quick technical breakdown inline to answer your points.

> 1) Sample invoice for committed = 1M tokens and we hit 1.35M?

See attached sample invoice rows (proposed-surge-pricing.xlsx). Roughly: committed invoice covers the committed 1M tokens at the committed rate. The +30% buffer (300k tokens) is invoiced as reserved capacity (prorated for the 30-day window). Any consumption beyond committed + buffer (so above 1.3M) is billed as overrun at the overrun tier described (first 50% of overrun delta at 1.6x, remainder at 2.4x). Example: 1.35M -> 50k tokens billed at 1.6x overrun.

> 2) Warm pool trigger and fallback

The warm pool is consumed first automatically. Once warm pool is depleted the system will fall back to payg headroom with the overrun rates above. There is no manual intervention required; autoscaling policies are configurable — we can set a hard throttle at your preference or permit fallback for uninterrupted traffic. We recommend fallback for user experience unless you want to enforce strict throttles.

> 3) Latency SLO impact

Routing to payg fallback may route to slightly smaller model variants or different instance sizes which can increase p95 by ~30–60ms in our tests for similar seq lengths. For most interactive Launchly flows the user impact is negligible, but we can pin the same model variant in the warm pool if you want latency parity at higher cost.

Attached: provisioning-plan.pdf which includes warm pool sizing and autoscale knob suggestions.

Happy to run a short test with your team during a quiet window.

Thanks,
